generator.vocabulary_is_closed: every state written here is a key of `states` below. A document whose Status string is not in that vocabulary is `unknown`, never a new category.
generator.status_is_not_correctness: Status tracks whether a human has acted, never whether the content is right. This tool reads the string.

reading.toggle: uv run qm docs states --state draft
reading.unknown_convention: {"unknown": "<reason>"} is a value, and `state: unknown` means the state could not be established. It is not `standing`, not `draft`, and not fine.
do_not: read `ratified` off a filename alone -- the Status row is the claim
read `proposed` as reviewed: nothing in this corpus has been ratified
treat `standing` as a state; it is the absence of one for that class
quote a count without this document's generated_at

states.draft: pre-ratification. Rewritten in place, binds nobody, and may change entirely.
states.proposed: drafted and awaiting a human's ratification. Binds nobody yet.
states.ratified: a human ratified it. This binds every QM project.
states.unreviewed: written, and no maintainer has looked at it. Opinion, never binding.
states.acknowledged: a maintainer has read it. Logged, no further commitment.
states.responded: concrete work exists because of it.
states.declined: a maintainer read it and decided not to act, for a stated reason.
states.generated: written by a tool. Do not edit by hand; check its age before quoting.
states.standing: policy or charter with no lifecycle defined for its class.
states.transient: working instructions, deleted when the work lands.
states.unknown: the state could not be established, which is not the same as fine.

reading_load.the_budget_is_a_ratchet: It is lowered as prose is deleted, never raised on contact. Raising it is an amendment to that record, argued in the open.

claim.name: alpha
claim.previous_phase_note: Everything merged on 2026-08-14/15 -- the two-gate correction, the qm CLI, four new gates, three generated layers, and the documentation. plans/v0.0.1-review-packet.md is what a human reviews to decide whether it earns a tag. Until that review happens it is a clean main and asserts nothing, per records/DRAFT-version-tags-are-claims.md 4.
claim.phase_note: v0.0.2 is language and review: whether governance prose invites a second author, and the first semantic reading of the records. Both are stubs in plans/ and neither is built.
claim.audience: Developers and power users outside QM, onboarded as testers. They read the corpus cold, with none of the session history that built it.

requires.what: At least one record ratified end to end, so the five-step path has been walked once
Mandatory reading before a first edit stays under its budget
Every governed document's state can be established
No gate is declared and unbuilt, or the gap is deliberate and named
All records read in one sitting for contradiction, which no check can do
requires.measured_by: not mechanisable -- a human says so, in a handoff or a record

readiness.claim_is_not_evidence: milestone, target_version and requires are what a human stated in ci/workspace.yaml. Nothing here is derived from the repository.

gates.unknown: held in gate-status.json, which this generator does not read -- one document does not restate another's figures

semantic_review.unknown: not mechanisable. A human reads every record in one sitting and says so; no count here can stand in for that

readiness.no_score_is_computed: This layer does not say whether the milestone is met. It puts the claim and the measurements side by side; the judgement is a human's, and one of the five requirements cannot be measured at all.
